newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS KEEP SIX-POINT LEAD AS UDINESE WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS KEEP SIX-POINT LEAD AS UDINESE WIN.

text.p: Juventus stayed six points clear in Italy's serie A on Sunday after Udinese, who beat them 3-0 in Turin last weekend, pulled off another stunning away win at second-placed Parma.

Mid-table Udinese, enjoying the role of serie A levellers, dealt Parma a devastating 2-0 defeat with a 66th minute close-range goal by defender Alessandro Pierini and an 87th minute penalty by German international Oliver Bierhoff.
European Cup holders Juventus, who beat Bologna 1-0 on Saturday and play Ajax Amsterdam in a Cup semifinal second leg in Turin on Wednesday, have 55 points.

Parma have 49 points and are now under increasing pressure from Internazionale, who beat Cagliari 2-1 in Sardinia on Saturday, and are snapping at their heels with 48 points in a battle for Italy's second European Cup slot next season.
In other matches, AC Milan's poor form continued with a 0-0 draw against lowly Piacenza at San Siro after Italy midfielder Demetrio Albertini missed a first half penalty.
Striker Igor Protti scored a first half hat-trick in the space of 15 minutes as Lazio thrashed bottom team Reggiana 6-1. Czech midfielder Pavel Nedved also scored twice.
Struggling Perugia lost 4-1 to Vicenza, playing in neutral Reggio Emilia, and finished the match with nine men.
